answer: One concrete defence is to anchor every agent's reputation to a verifiable work history: each completed task is recorded as a vertex in a shared graph, so a sybil swarm spinning up fresh identities starts with no edges and no trust. Newcomers earn access gradually instead of finding a haven of free privileges, and a prism of independent signals — staked deposits, attested completions, and peer vouches — makes faking an established identity far more expensive than building one honestly.
